The path is divided into 12 periods, each lasting 4-6 weeks, and covers a range of topics from data literacy and data science to machine learning, deep learning, and data engineering. The path is designed to be challenging but not overwhelming, with a mix of theoretical concepts, practical exercises, and real-world projects to maintain engagement and motivation. Regular assessments and feedback mechanisms are built into the path to help the learner identify areas of strength and weakness, and adjust their learning strategy accordingly.

**Learning Path**

| Period | Course ID | Course Title | Platform | Why this course |

| 1 | EDX3413 | Managing Technical Professionals | edx | Foundational knowledge of different management approaches and conflict resolution. |
| 2 | EDX2890 | Teamwork & Collaboration | edx | Building on the previous course, this one focuses on teamwork and collaboration, essential for effective leadership. |
| 3 | EDX3423 | Leadership Program | edx | Introducing leadership principles and skills, this course provides a solid foundation for the learner to build on. |
| 4 | EDX3400 | Women’s Leadership Program: Leading Teams | edx | Emphasizing soft skills, this course helps the learner develop essential leadership skills, such as communication and conflict resolution. |
| 5 | EDX3417 | Leadership in an Exponentially Changing World | edx | This advanced course focuses on leading in a rapidly changing environment, helping the learner develop a more proactive leadership style. |
| 6 | EDX3283 | Oxford Leading Strategic Projects Programme | edx | This final course provides a comprehensive toolkit for leading strategic projects, incorporating the skills and knowledge acquired throughout the learning path. |

**How the path fits together**

This learning path provides a structured approach to developing leadership skills, starting with foundational knowledge of management approaches and conflict resolution. The path then builds on this foundation, introducing teamwork and collaboration, leadership principles, and essential soft skills. The final two courses focus on leading in a rapidly changing environment and leading strategic projects, providing a comprehensive toolkit for effective leadership. Throughout the path, the learner is encouraged to develop self-awareness, reflection, and metacognition skills, ensuring they can recognize their strengths and weaknesses, set realistic goals, and adapt to changing team dynamics.

learning_path:
**Learning Path**

| Period | Course ID | Course Title | Platform | Why this course |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | EDX2909 | Principles of Electric Circuits | edx | Foundational course on electric circuits, covering math basics and circuit analysis. |
| 2 | EDX509 | Circuits for Beginners | edx | Builds on EDX2909, introducing circuit analysis methods and electrical measurement equipment. |
| 3 | EDX478 | Circuits and Electronics 1: Basic Circuit Analysis | edx | Expands on EDX509, covering lumped circuit models, abstraction, and intuition-based problem-solving. |
| 4 | EDX861 | Circuits and Electronics 2: Amplification, Speed, and Delay | edx | Develops the learner's understanding of amplifiers, energy storage elements, and real-life effects. |
| 5 | EDX1435 | Circuits and Electronics 3: Applications | edx | Applies circuit analysis to real-world scenarios, including filters, op-amps, and digital circuits. |
| 6 | EDX206 | AC and Switching Circuits | edx | Introduces AC circuits, RMS voltage and current, and handling non-sinusoidal sources. |
| 7 | EDX361 | Electromagnetic Compatibility Essentials | edx | Covers electromagnetic interference (EMI) and noise control techniques. |
| 8 | EDX981 | Electricity & Magnetism, Part 2 | edx | Expands on electromagnetic concepts, including magnetic fields, induction, and inductors. |
| 9 | EDX2786 | Linear Algebra I: Vectors and Linear Equations | edx | Introduces linear algebra concepts, including vectors, linear equations, and matrix operations. |
| 10 | EDX2180 | Linear Algebra II: Matrices and Linear Transformations | edx | Develops the learner's understanding of matrix operations, eigenvalues, and eigenvectors. |

The learning path starts with EDX2909, which provides a foundational understanding of electric circuits. EDX509 builds on this, introducing circuit analysis methods and electrical measurement equipment. EDX478 expands on EDX509, covering lumped circuit models, abstraction, and intuition-based problem-solving. EDX861 develops the learner's understanding of amplifiers, energy storage elements, and real-life effects. EDX1435 applies circuit analysis to real-world scenarios, including filters, op-amps, and digital circuits. EDX206 introduces AC circuits, RMS voltage and current, and handling non-sinusoidal sources. EDX361 covers electromagnetic interference (EMI) and noise control techniques. EDX981 expands on electromagnetic concepts, including magnetic fields, induction, and inductors. EDX2786 introduces linear algebra concepts, including vectors, linear equations, and matrix operations. | 6 | COU1613 | Instructional Methods in Health Professions Education | Coursera | This course focuses on instructional methods, specifically in health professions education, allowing the learner to apply their knowledge in a practical context. |
| 7 | EDX2145 | Shifting Your Teaching Online | edX | As the learner transitions to online teaching, this course equips them with the skills to deliver engaging online content and support students effectively. |

Each course builds on the previous one, providing a cohesive and structured learning experience for the new teacher. The path culminates in a capstone project, where the learner applies their knowledge and skills to create a comprehensive teaching plan.

Period 5 introduces object-oriented design and software construction principles. Period 6 is a capstone project, where the learner applies their knowledge to build a full-stack web application using Typescript and Node.js. Finally, Period 7 introduces RISC-V assembly programming, which is not directly related to mobile app development but provides a deeper understanding of programming concepts.

| 9 | EDX207 | Machine Learning with Python: from Linear Models to Deep Learning | edx | Advanced machine learning concepts |
| 10 | EDX2849 | Probability and Statistics in Data Science using Python | edx | Probability and statistics in data science |

## Path Explanation

This learning path starts with foundational courses in probability and inference, then introduces machine learning concepts, and gradually builds up to advanced machine learning and data science topics. The path emphasizes mathematical rigor and Python implementation, and covers linear algebra and vector spaces, advanced linear algebra concepts, data science, and machine learning applications. The final course in the path covers probability and statistics in data science, providing a comprehensive understanding of the subject.

The path covers the full duration the learner asked for, with at least one course per period. The available courses do not fully cover the request, but the recommended courses provide a comprehensive understanding of linear algebra and probability, and their applications in machine learning.

learning_path:
**Learning Path for Business Writing and Professional Communication**

| Period | Course ID | Course Title | Platform | Why this course |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | EDX3082 | English for Doing Business in Asia – Speaking | edx | Develops foundational English language skills, including pronunciation, rhythm, and oral presentation skills, essential for business writing and professional communication. |
| 2 | EDX792 | Academic and Business Writing | edx | Builds on prior knowledge of English language skills, focusing on writing techniques, proofreading, self-editing, revision, tone, and vocabulary, which are critical for effective business writing. |
| 3 | EDX3277 | Professional Communication: Business Writing and Storytelling | edx | Expands on writing skills, introducing practical writing, editing, and data-visualisation skills for creating clear and compelling business communications, as well as a writer's toolkit for navigating structure, word choice, and style. |
| 4 | EDX2619 | Business Communications - The Basics | edx | Develops foundational communication skills, including defining communication, examining communication principles, identifying ways to effectively listen, and examining emotional intelligence in communication. |
| 5 | EDX2153 | Business Communication | edx | Focuses on critical evaluation of the role in workplace interactions, active listening, and effective communication of ideas, which are essential for professional communication. |
| 6 | EDX2077 | Business Writing Techniques | edx | Refines business writing skills, including identifying parts of a business letter, evaluating direct vs. indirect messages, and examining the use of emojis in the business setting. |

The learning path progresses from foundational English language skills (Period 1) to developing writing techniques and communication skills (Periods 2-4). Period 5 focuses on critical evaluation and effective communication, while Period 6 refines business writing skills. Each course builds on prior knowledge, gradually increasing cognitive load and emphasizing practical application. The path is designed to be culturally sensitive and inclusive, taking into account the learner's non-native English background.

This learning path starts with a review of limits and derivatives (COU4099) to ensure a strong foundation in calculus. The next course (COU288) builds on this foundation by covering differentiation rules, a crucial concept in calculus. The third course (COU4437) introduces functions, a fundamental concept in calculus, and provides a solid understanding of series expansions. With a solid grasp of functions and differentiation, the learner is ready to tackle advanced calculus topics, including differential equations and series representations (COU4065). Finally, this course applies advanced calculus concepts to machine learning and data science (COU75), making it relevant to the learner's future engineering degree. This path follows the educational principles of building on prior knowledge, gradual increase in cognitive load, emphasizing conceptual understanding, pacing and practice, motivation through relevance, and sequencing learning to build on skills.

## How the path fits together

This course path starts with a foundational understanding of probability and inference, introducing the learner to the mathematical concepts necessary for machine learning. The path continues with introducing Python programming and data analysis, and then building on data analysis to introduce machine learning fundamentals. Finally, the learner is introduced to predictive analytics and machine learning modeling techniques, and concludes with a course on machine learning with Python, from linear models to deep learning. This path provides a comprehensive understanding of linear algebra, probability, and machine learning, allowing the learner to follow machine learning papers with confidence.

This learning path starts with a foundational understanding of statistical concepts, including data analysis, linear regression, and statistical hypothesis testing (COU4426). Building on this understanding, the path introduces data analysis and visualization (COU5896), essential for interpreting research studies. The next course provides a comprehensive understanding of data science and its application in health research (COU4777), including data wrangling, logistic regression, and R coding. This is followed by a course that introduces machine learning and its application in data science (COU4983). To reinforce the learner's understanding of statistical concepts, the path includes a foundational course on statistics (COU5901). Finally, the path concludes with a course that helps the learner develop skills in interpreting statistical results, rather than just calculating them, and provides a comprehensive understanding of research evaluation (COU2744).

| Period | Course ID | Course Title | Platform | Why this course |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | COU923 | Getting Started With Music Theory | Coursera | Foundational music theory course to build on prior knowledge |
| 2 | COU4357 | Developing Your Musicianship Specialization | Coursera | Leverage music theory to develop musicianship skills |
| 3 | COU2512 | Approaching Music Theory: Melodic Forms and Simple Harmony | Coursera | Build on music theory and explore melodic forms and simple harmony |
| 4 | COU5891 | Music Production: Crafting Award-Worthy Songs Specialization | Coursera | Apply music theory and musicianship skills to music production |
| 5 | COU455 | FL Studio Basics | Coursera | Introduce digital audio workstation skills for music production |
| 6 | COU3163 | Music Production Specialization | Coursera | Develop music production skills and apply to real-world composing tasks |
| 7 | COU2108 | Developing Your Musicianship: Final Project | Coursera | Apply music theory, musicianship, and production skills to a final project |

This learning path starts with a foundational music theory course (COU923) to build on prior knowledge. The next course (COU4357) leverages music theory to develop musicianship skills. Course COU2512 builds on music theory and explores melodic forms and simple harmony. Course COU5891 applies music theory and musicianship skills to music production. **Learning Path for a Complete Beginner in Photography and Visual Design**
====================================================================

| Period | Course ID | Course Title | Platform | Why this course |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | COU5230 | Photography Basics and Beyond: From Smartphone to DSLR Specialization | Coursera | Introduces the basics of photography, including light, composition, and visual elements. |
| 2 | COU4519 | Photography Capstone Project | Coursera | Allows the learner to apply their new skills through a practical project, receiving feedback and developing a sense of accomplishment. |
| 3 | COU5235 | Graphic Design Elements for Non-Designers Specialization | Coursera | Introduces the fundamentals of graphic design, including color theory, typography, and visual elements. |
| 4 | COU4668 | Graphic Design Fundamentals | Coursera | Develops the learner's understanding of visual principles, creative problem-solving, and critical thinking. |
| 5 | COU1471 | Graphic Design | Coursera | Focuses on developing transferable skills, such as understanding of visual principles, creative problem-solving, and critical thinking. |
| 6 | COU3986 | Agile Development Specialization | Coursera | Introduces the learner to design thinking and how it is used in UX/UI design, allowing them to develop a portfolio of their designs. |
| 7 | COU3968 | Fundamentals of UI/UX Design | Coursera | Develops the learner's understanding of user experience design (UXD) and human-centered design (HCD), allowing them to create a portfolio of their designs. |
| 8 | COU1298 | Design Thinking Specialization | Coursera | Focuses on developing the learner's strategic thinking, creativity, and innovation skills, allowing them to create a unique visual voice. |

**How the path fits together**

This learning path is designed to take a complete beginner in photography and visual design from the basics of photography to advanced design thinking and UX/UI design. The path starts with the basics of photography, including light, composition, and visual elements (COU5230). The learner then applies their new skills through a practical project, receiving feedback and developing a sense of accomplishment (COU4519). Next, the learner is introduced to the fundamentals of graphic design, including color theory, typography, and visual elements (COU5235). The learner then develops their understanding of visual principles, creative problem-solving, and critical thinking (COU4668). The path continues with a focus on developing transferable skills, such as understanding of visual principles, creative problem-solving, and critical thinking (COU1471). The learner is then introduced to design thinking and how it is used in UX/UI design, allowing them to develop a portfolio of their designs (COU3986). Finally, the learner develops their understanding of user experience design (UXD) and human-centered design (HCD), allowing them to create a unique visual voice (COU3968).

The final two periods focus on self-directed learning, time management, and community-supported learning, with a practical application of these skills in a human resources context. **Learning Path**

| Period | Course ID | Course Title | Platform | Why this course |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | COU1458 | English Language Skills A2-B1 CEFR: Low-Intermediate Specialization | Coursera | Foundational course to establish a solid base in English language skills, including grammar, vocabulary, and reading comprehension. |
| 2 | COU4837 | Low Intermediate English: Help & Information | Coursera | Builds on the foundational course, focusing on important language for asking for help, giving and understanding directions, and sharing opinions. |
| 3 | COU6106 | Business English Communication Skills Specialization | Coursera | Introduces business English communication skills, including vocabulary, grammar, and listening comprehension, to prepare the learner for more advanced technical communication skills. |
| 4 | COU1609 | Business English: Networking | Coursera | Develops the learner's ability to communicate effectively in a business setting, including email writing, business communication, and networking. |
| 5 | COU2362 | English for Effective Business Speaking | Coursera | Focuses on improving the learner's business English speaking skills, including vocabulary, grammar, pronunciation, and spoken communication skills. |
| 6 | COU4648 | Low Intermediate English: Calls & Messaging | Coursera | Enhances the learner's ability to communicate effectively in a business setting, including phone, email, text, and social media communication. |
| 7 | COU2201 | Low Intermediate English: Shopping & Customer Service | Coursera | Develops the learner's language skills for describing how to shop, review what's been bought, and assist customers, preparing them for more advanced customer service skills. |
| 8 | COU4252 | Low Intermediate English: Planning & Organization | Coursera | Focuses on the learner's ability to plan their life, including social life, travels, and work, using important language for planning and organization. |
| 9 | COU5945 | English for Effective Business Writing | Coursera | Improves the learner's business English writing skills, including vocabulary, grammar, and understanding of different business writing genres. |
| 10 | COU2975 | Arizona State University TESOL Professional Certificate | Coursera | Provides a beginner-level course in English language teaching, preparing the learner for more advanced teaching and communication skills. |

The learning path progresses from foundational to advanced, covering the full duration of the learner's request. Each course builds on the previous one, introducing new skills and concepts in a gradual and manageable way. The path emphasizes practical application, motivation through relevance and feedback, and flexibility and adaptability to accommodate the learner's individual needs.
